statement: Cardiorespiratory fitness (VO2max), best measured directly by cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) and approximated by treadmill/cycle time or submaximal/non-exercise equations, is recommended as a clinical 'vital sign': it adds prognostic information beyond traditional risk factors and is the single strongest exercise-related predictor of all-cause mortality.
effect_size: CRF reclassifies mortality risk beyond standard factors; AHA recommends routine assessment. (Magnitude itself: see Mandsager ~5x, Kodama ~13%/MET in E-claims.)
population: AHA Scientific Statement synthesizing large CRF-mortality cohorts

provenance.primary: Ross, Blair, Arena, Church et al. — 'Importance of Assessing Cardiorespiratory Fitness in Clinical Practice: A Case for Fitness as a Clinical Vital Sign', Circulation 2016

confidence_notes: Measurement-side companion to E-claims crf-vo2max-strongest-mortality-predictor and crf-per-met-mortality-meta (the magnitude lives there). Honest caveat: directly-measured (CPET) and treadmill-time CRF carry the mortality data; consumer-wearable and non-exercise ESTIMATED VO2max are substantially less accurate (large individual error), so they are trend tools, not calibrated risk instruments.

statement: Bone mineral density measured by DEXA predicts osteoporotic fracture: each 1-SD decrease in BMD is associated with roughly a 1.5-3x increase in fracture risk (site-specific measurement predicts that site best), making DXA the reference test for osteoporosis diagnosis.
effect_size: Relative risk ~1.5 per SD for general fracture, up to ~2.6 for hip BMD predicting hip fracture.
population: Meta-analysis of prospective BMD-fracture cohorts (~90,000 person-years)

provenance.primary: Marshall, Johnell, Wedel — 'Meta-analysis of how well measures of bone mineral density predict occurrence of osteoporotic fractures', BMJ 1996

confidence_notes: Strong predictor but with a key limitation the headline hides: because most people fall in the non-osteoporotic BMD range, the MAJORITY of fragility fractures occur in people whose BMD is not in the osteoporotic range (low sensitivity). Hence FRAX-style tools combine BMD with clinical risk factors. Gradient is robust; single-threshold screening misses most events.

statement: DXA-measured muscle (lean) mass does NOT independently predict mortality once muscle STRENGTH is accounted for; low strength predicts death whereas low lean mass largely does not — so body-composition mass alone is a weaker longevity biomarker than function.
effect_size: Quadriceps/grip strength associated with mortality (top vs bottom tertile HR materially lower); DXA-measured lean/muscle mass NOT independently associated after adjusting for strength and fat.
population: Health, Aging and Body Composition Study, ~2,292 adults aged 70-79, ~4.9y follow-up

provenance.primary: Newman, Kupelian, Visser, Simonsick et al. — 'Strength, But Not Muscle Mass, Is Associated With Mortality in the Health, Aging and Body Composition Study Cohort', J Gerontol A Biol Sci Med Sci 2006
provenance.surfaced_via: OpenAlex search (DXA appendicular lean mass sarcopenia)

confidence_notes: The empirical basis for the EWGSOP2 shift from mass to strength (see E-claims sarcopenia-strength-defining-ewgsop2). Practical implication: DXA is excellent for BONE and for tracking fat distribution, but for longevity the cheap strength/function tests (grip, gait, chair-rise) out-predict the expensive lean-mass scan.

statement: Visceral adipose tissue (VAT) is an independent predictor of all-cause mortality, adding risk information beyond BMI, total fat and waist circumference; central/visceral adiposity is metabolically harmful in a way total body weight is not.
effect_size: Higher VAT associated with elevated all-cause mortality independent of total adiposity (men).
population: ~291 men, mortality follow-up, VAT by imaging (Kuk/Katzmarzyk)

provenance.primary: Kuk, Katzmarzyk, Nichaman, Church, Blair, Ross — 'Visceral Fat Is an Independent Predictor of All-cause Mortality in Men', Obesity 2006
provenance.surfaced_via: OpenAlex search (visceral adipose tissue mortality); initial DOI .34 collided, corrected to .43

confidence_notes: Modest sample, men only; CT/MRI are the imaging reference standard for VAT while DXA VAT is an ESTIMATE (good correlation, not interchangeable). Supports tracking fat DISTRIBUTION over scale weight; cross-links to metabolic-health Domain D (insulin resistance, ectopic fat).

statement: Usual gait speed predicts survival in older adults across the whole range of speeds, comparably to a model using age, sex, chronic conditions, smoking, blood pressure and hospitalization; each 0.1 m/s faster gait is associated with meaningfully lower mortality.
effect_size: Per 0.1 m/s higher gait speed: ~12% lower mortality hazard; predicted survival varied widely (e.g. ~19% to ~87% 10-yr survival) by speed within age/sex strata.
population: Pooled analysis of 9 cohorts, ~34,485 community-dwelling adults aged >=65

provenance.primary: Studenski, Perera, Patel, Guralnik et al. — 'Gait Speed and Survival in Older Adults', JAMA 2011

confidence_notes: Large pooled cohort — among the cheapest, most reproducible biomarkers in geriatrics (a stopwatch over 4 m). BIOMARKER of integrated health (cardiopulmonary, neuromuscular, cognitive), not proof that walking faster on command lowers mortality; reverse causation (subclinical disease slows gait) contributes. Cross-ref grip-strength-mortality-pure (E).

statement: Meta-analysis of prospective cohorts confirms slow gait speed is associated with higher all-cause and cardiovascular mortality, validating gait speed as a generalizable prognostic biomarker beyond any single cohort.
effect_size: Slowest vs fastest gait speed associated with substantially higher all-cause and CVD mortality (pooled).
population: Systematic review + meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies

provenance.primary: Veronese, Stubbs, Volpato et al. — 'Association Between Gait Speed With Mortality, Cardiovascular Disease and Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Prospective Cohort Studies', J Am Med Dir Assoc 2018

confidence_notes: Meta of OBSERVATIONAL cohorts. Confirms direction/generalizability; same reverse-causation caveat as Studenski.

statement: Objectively measured physical capability — grip strength, walking/gait speed, chair-rise (sit-to-stand) time and standing balance — each independently predicts all-cause mortality in community populations; simple performance tests are robust, low-cost biomarkers of survival.
effect_size: Weakest vs strongest grip HR ~1.67; slowest vs fastest gait HR ~2.87; slowest vs fastest chair-rise HR ~1.96; worst vs best balance HR ~2.14 (pooled).
population: Systematic review + meta-analysis, dozens of cohorts, >50,000 participants

provenance.primary: Cooper, Kuh, Hardy et al. — 'Objectively measured physical capability levels and mortality: systematic review and meta-analysis', BMJ 2010

confidence_notes: The omnibus meta tying together the cheap functional biomarkers. Extends grip-strength-mortality-pure (E, PURE/Leong) to a broader battery. All observational; capability is a READOUT of integrated organ-system reserve. The practical headline: four stopwatch/dynamometer tests rival expensive panels for prognosis.

statement: Apolipoprotein B (apoB), which counts the number of atherogenic lipoprotein particles, is a more accurate marker of cardiovascular risk than LDL-cholesterol (which measures cholesterol mass); when apoB and LDL-C disagree (discordance — common in high-triglyceride, diabetic and metabolic-syndrome states), risk tracks apoB (particle number), not LDL-C.
effect_size: ApoB outperforms LDL-C and non-HDL-C in head-to-head risk discrimination; in discordance analyses apoB-defined risk dominates. Marston 2022: apoB-containing particle number drives MI risk in and out of established atherosclerosis.
population: Meta-analyses + large cohorts (Sniderman reviews; Marston UK Biobank/FOURIER analyses)

provenance.primary: Sniderman, Thanassoulis, Glavinovic et al. — 'Apolipoprotein B Particles and Cardiovascular Disease: A Narrative Review', JAMA Cardiology 2019; Sniderman et al. — 'A Meta-Analysis of LDL-C, non-HDL-C, and ApoB as Markers of Cardiovascular Risk', Circ Cardiovasc Qual Outcomes 2011 (10.1161/circoutcomes.110.959247); Marston et al., JAMA Cardiol 2022 (10.1001/jamacardio.2021.5083)

confidence_notes: Strong, convergent evidence apoB is the better METRIC. Practical: one apoB measure subsumes LDL-C/non-HDL/particle-count debates. Still observational for risk DISCRIMINATION; the CAUSAL claim is separate (see ldl-apob-causal-ascvd). LDL-C remains the historical guideline target mainly for inertia/assay availability.

statement: LDL and other apoB-containing lipoproteins are CAUSAL for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease — established by triangulating genetic (Mendelian randomization), epidemiologic and randomized-trial evidence — and the effect depends on cumulative lifetime exposure (area under the apoB-x-time curve), not just current level.
effect_size: Dose-dependent, log-linear, cumulative causal relationship; multivariable MR isolates apoB as the causal lipid trait (LDL-C/TG effects attenuate to apoB).
population: EAS consensus synthesis (genetic + epi + RCT) + multivariable MR (UK Biobank etc.)

provenance.primary: Ference, Ginsberg, Graham, Ray et al. — 'Low-density lipoproteins cause atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease... A consensus statement from the EAS', Eur Heart J 2017; Richardson et al. — multivariable MR, PLoS Med 2020 (10.1371/journal.pmed.1003062)

confidence_notes: One of the FEW genuinely CAUSAL (not merely associational) outcome claims in this whole corpus — earns its tier because genetics + RCT + epi all converge. The cumulative-exposure framing is why early/lifelong apoB lowering matters more than late correction. This is the highest-confidence modifiable blood biomarker.

statement: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a genetically-determined, causal risk factor for myocardial infarction, coronary and aortic-valve disease: genetic variants raising Lp(a) raise event risk (Mendelian randomization), and the level is ~70-90% heritable and largely stable through life — so it need only be measured once.
effect_size: Top vs bottom Lp(a)/LPA-genotype tertiles: ~2x+ MI risk; risk rises with LPA kringle-IV-type-2 copy number / corrected for genotype.
population: Copenhagen City Heart Study + genetic cohorts (Kamstrup); PROCARDIS genetic study (Clarke)

provenance.primary: Kamstrup, Tybjaerg-Hansen, Steffensen, Nordestgaard — 'Genetically Elevated Lipoprotein(a) and Increased Risk of Myocardial Infarction', JAMA 2009; Clarke et al. — 'Genetic Variants Associated with Lp(a) Lipoprotein Level and Coronary Disease', NEJM 2009

confidence_notes: Causal via MR (genetics fix the level, so confounding/reverse-causation are excluded). Practically: a once-in-a-lifetime test that identifies a high-risk subgroup (~20% of people) currently with no approved Lp(a)-specific therapy (RNA-targeted agents in trials). High measurement value, limited intervention value as of 2026.

statement: High-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) predicts coronary heart disease, stroke and vascular mortality as a marker of systemic inflammation, but Mendelian randomization shows CRP itself is NOT causal — it is a readout of the inflammatory state, not a lever to pull.
effect_size: Predictive: per ~1-SD higher log-CRP, CHD risk ratio ~1.37 (adjusted, Kaptoge/ERFC). Causal: CRP genetic variants that raise CRP do NOT raise CHD risk (null MR, CCGC 2011).
population: ERFC: 160,000+ participants, 54 prospective studies (predictive); CCGC: 47 studies / 194,418 individuals (Mendelian randomization)

provenance.primary: Kaptoge et al. (Emerging Risk Factors Collaboration) — 'C-reactive protein concentration and risk of CHD, stroke, and mortality: an individual participant meta-analysis', Lancet 2010; C-Reactive Protein CHD Genetics Collaboration — 'Association between CRP and CHD: mendelian randomisation analysis', BMJ 2011

confidence_notes: Textbook predictor-vs-cause case and a discipline anchor for this domain: hsCRP is a USEFUL risk marker (cheap, tracks inflammaging — cross-ref C iAge/CXCL9) but lowering CRP per se is not the goal; the JUPITER RCT (Ridker 2008, 10.1056/NEJMoa0807646) used hsCRP to SELECT patients but benefit came via LDL/apoB lowering, not CRP reduction. Grade direction 'mixed' precisely because predictive!=causal.

statement: HbA1c (glycated hemoglobin, a 2-3 month average of blood glucose) predicts cardiovascular disease and all-cause mortality even within the non-diabetic range, and does so at least as well as — with practical advantages over — fasting glucose.
effect_size: Vs HbA1c 5.0-5.4%: at 6.0-6.5% (non-diabetic) adjusted HR for CVD ~1.4-1.9 and for death elevated; J/threshold shape with risk rising above ~5.5-6.0%.
population: ARIC study, ~11,092 non-diabetic Black and White adults, ~14-15y follow-up

provenance.primary: Selvin, Steffes, Zhu, Matsushita et al. — 'Glycated Hemoglobin, Diabetes, and Cardiovascular Risk in Nondiabetic Adults', NEJM 2010

confidence_notes: Cohort. HbA1c integrates glycemia over months (less day-to-day noise than a single fasting glucose) and needs no fasting. Caveats: distorted by anything changing red-cell lifespan (anemia, hemoglobinopathies, recent blood loss) — a real false-signal source. Cross-ref Domain D metabolic claims.

statement: Fasting plasma glucose is associated with vascular disease risk in a threshold/J-shaped manner: risk is roughly flat across the normal range and rises above ~5.6 mmol/L (~100 mg/dL), with diabetes itself roughly doubling vascular risk.
effect_size: Diabetes: ~2x vascular disease HR; non-diabetic fasting glucose <~5.6 mmol/L largely non-linear/weak; modest rise in the impaired-fasting-glucose band.
population: Emerging Risk Factors Collaboration: 102 prospective studies, ~698,782 individuals

provenance.primary: Emerging Risk Factors Collaboration — 'Diabetes mellitus, fasting blood glucose concentration, and risk of vascular disease: a collaborative meta-analysis of 102 prospective studies', Lancet 2010

confidence_notes: Meta-tier for fasting glucose. The flat-then-rising shape matters: a single fasting glucose in the normal range is reassuring but low-resolution. HbA1c and HOMA-IR/fasting insulin catch dysmetabolism earlier (insulin rises years before glucose). Cross-ref Domain D.

statement: Insulin resistance quantified by HOMA-IR (from fasting glucose x fasting insulin) predicts incident cardiovascular disease, and fasting hyperinsulinemia is an early marker of metabolic dysfunction that rises years before fasting glucose or HbA1c become abnormal.
effect_size: Higher HOMA-IR associated with greater incident CVD independent of other risk factors (top vs bottom strata elevated HR).
population: Insulin Resistance Atherosclerosis Study (IRAS) / San Antonio Heart Study, non-diabetic adults

provenance.primary: Hanley, Williams, Stern, Haffner et al. — 'Homeostasis Model Assessment of Insulin Resistance in Relation to the Incidence of Cardiovascular Disease', Diabetes Care 2002

confidence_notes: Cohort. The main practical caveat is ASSAY: insulin immunoassays are poorly standardized between labs, so HOMA-IR cut-points are not universally portable (track within-person trend on one assay). Conceptually the earliest-warning metabolic biomarker; cross-ref Domain D (insulin sensitivity, CGM).

statement: Circulating IGF-1 has a U-shaped (non-monotonic) relationship with mortality: BOTH low and high IGF-1 are associated with higher all-cause and cardiovascular mortality, so 'lower IGF-1 = longer life' (the simple extrapolation from worm/mouse insulin/IGF longevity genetics) does not hold cleanly in humans.
effect_size: Both tails of the IGF-1 distribution carry excess mortality (dose-response metaregression); the safest zone is mid-range, not lowest.
population: Meta-analysis + dose-response metaregression of circulating IGF-1 and mortality

provenance.primary: Burgers, Biermasz, Schoones, Pereira et al. — 'Meta-Analysis and Dose-Response Metaregression: Circulating Insulin-Like Growth Factor I (IGF-I) and Mortality', J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2011

confidence_notes: Directly tempers naive 'suppress IGF-1/mTOR for longevity' biohacking and links to the protein/mTOR conflict (Domain D) and GH/IGF-1 longevity genetics (Bartke, Laron — C/D). As a tracked biomarker IGF-1 is a context-dependent dial (cancer/anabolism tradeoff), not a 'minimize' target.

statement: Epigenetic / biological-age tests (Horvath, PhenoAge, GrimAge, DunedinPACE and consumer derivatives) predict mortality and morbidity at the population level, but NONE is yet a validated surrogate endpoint: no test is proven to MOVE with an intervention in a way that reliably forecasts that intervention's clinical benefit, and first-generation clocks have measurement-reliability problems that make individual 'age reversal' readings untrustworthy.
effect_size: Population-level mortality prediction is real (2nd-gen clocks strongest); individual-level reliability is low for original clocks (ICC up to PC-clock fix), and surrogate validity is unestablished by consensus.
population: Biomarkers of Aging Consortium consensus + reliability re-analyses (cross-domain)

provenance.primary: Moqri, Herzog, Gladyshev et al. — 'Biomarkers of aging for the identification and evaluation of longevity interventions', Cell 2023 (10.1016/j.cell.2023.08.003); Higgins-Chen et al., Nat Aging 2022 (PC-clocks, 10.1038/s43587-022-00248-2)
provenance.surfaced_via: Cross-ref Domain C (biomarkers-of-aging-consortium-validation-gap, higgins-chen-2022-pc-clocks, marioni-2015-dnam-age-mortality, chen-2016-dnam-meta-mortality)

confidence_notes: This is the measurement-side restatement of Domain C's central finding, placed in L because consumers BUY these tests to make decisions. Honest verdict: useful research/population biomarker; premature and noisy as a personal scorecard for judging whether your protocol is 'working'. Use trend over many measures, never a single number.

statement: Reduced heart-rate variability (HRV) — a readout of cardiac autonomic (vagal/parasympathetic) tone — predicts all-cause and cardiac mortality in population cohorts; lower HRV signals worse autonomic regulation and higher risk.
effect_size: Lower HRV (e.g. low SDNN) associated with elevated mortality hazard over follow-up (Framingham elderly cohort).
population: Framingham Heart Study elderly cohort (~736 subjects, ~4y); replicated in later/larger cohorts

provenance.primary: Tsuji, Venditti, Manders, Evans et al. — 'Reduced heart rate variability and mortality risk in an elderly cohort. The Framingham Heart Study', Circulation 1994

confidence_notes: Cohort biomarker. BIG measurement caveat: HRV is highly variable and method/context dependent (metric chosen, recording length, posture, breathing, time of day, age) — see Shaffer & Ginsberg 2017 norms (10.3389/fpubh.2017.00258). Consumer overnight HRV (Oura/Whoop/Garmin) is a WITHIN-PERSON trend/recovery tool, NOT a calibrated cross-person mortality instrument; absolute values are not comparable between people or devices. Cross-ref Domains G (breath) and I (sleep/recovery).

statement: Consumer sleep trackers estimate total sleep time and basic sleep/wake reasonably well but are unreliable for sleep STAGING (light/deep/REM) and sleep architecture when compared against polysomnography, the clinical gold standard.
effect_size: Devices track sleep/wake and total sleep time with moderate agreement; stage-classification accuracy (especially deep and REM) is substantially worse and varies by device.
population: Head-to-head validation of 7 consumer devices vs in-lab PSG in healthy adults (Chinoy 2021)

provenance.primary: Chinoy, Cuellar, Huwa, Jameson et al. — 'Performance of seven consumer sleep-tracking devices compared with polysomnography', SLEEP 2021

confidence_notes: Validity/measurement claim. Practical: trust your tracker's DURATION and consistency (bed/wake timing) signal; treat its 'deep sleep %' and stage breakdown as approximate. Useful for behavior change (timing, regularity), not for diagnosing sleep disorders. Cross-ref Domain I.

statement: Modern continuous glucose monitors are accurate enough for diabetes management (reported MARD ~9-10%), but sensor-to-sensor and sensor-vs-blood disagreement is non-trivial, and CGM is NOT validated to improve health OUTCOMES in non-diabetic ('worried-well') users — the wellness use case rests on glucose variability that has no proven outcome benefit in healthy people.
effect_size: Accuracy varies materially across sensors/conditions (Kovatchev: numerical+clinical accuracy differ across 4 devices); validated metric is time-in-range for diabetes (Danne consensus). No outcome RCT in healthy people.
population: Head-to-head CGM accuracy comparison (Kovatchev 2008) + international CGM consensus (Danne 2017)

provenance.primary: Kovatchev, Anderson, Heinemann, Clarke — 'Comparison of the Numerical and Clinical Accuracy of Four Continuous Glucose Monitors', Diabetes Care 2008; Danne et al. — 'International Consensus on Use of Continuous Glucose Monitoring', Diabetes Care 2017

confidence_notes: Measurement-side companion to Domain D's conflict-cgm-healthy-utility. Honest split: genuine, validated tool in diabetes (time-in-range is consensus); unproven gadget for healthy biohackers, where two sensors on the same person can disagree and 'spikes' have no demonstrated outcome meaning. Real tool, oversold market.

statement: The inability to complete a 10-second one-legged (single-leg) stance is associated with higher all-cause mortality in middle-aged and older adults, and adds prognostic information beyond age, sex, BMI and comorbidities — making a simple, equipment-free balance test a mortality biomarker.
effect_size: Inability to complete 10-s OLS: adjusted HR for all-cause mortality 1.84 (95% CI 1.23-2.78). 20.4% could not complete it; over median 7y follow-up 17.5% of 'NO' vs 4.6% of 'YES' died. Adding 10-s OLS to established risk factors significantly improved mortality prediction (IDI).
population: 1702 individuals aged 51-75 (68% men), Brazil (CLINIMEX), assessed 2008-2020, median 7y follow-up

provenance.primary: Araujo, Silva, Laukkanen, Fiatarone Singh, Kunutsor et al. — 'Successful 10-second one-legged stance performance predicts survival in middle-aged and older individuals', British Journal of Sports Medicine 2022
provenance.surfaced_via: OpenAlex direct-DOI (Wave 4; flagged not-yet-graded in MOVEMENT-EVIDENCE.md single-leg-balance row)

confidence_notes: Completes the five 'movement biomarkers' set (joins gait-speed-survival-studenski, physical-capability-battery-mortality-meta, sit-to-rise-mortality [J], grip strength [E]). Single cohort, mostly men, one center (CLINIMEX/Brazil) — less validated than gait speed (pooled cohorts). Same reverse-causation caveat: subclinical disease/frailty impairs balance, so the test is a READOUT of integrated neuromuscular/vestibular/cognitive reserve, not proof that practicing balance lowers mortality. Pairs with movement-library single-leg-balance demonstration (the measurement and the trainable movement collapse into one object).
